chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Spending money in Holland and rumors of Hitler
summary: The band arrived in Holland in fezzes with Egyptian spoils, was jailed for spending too fast, played a Dutch engagement and heard rumors about Hitler at the end of 1936 and in 1937.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: (Den Haag?) Dieve, Holland, now we comes into Holland with them fezes on. Fezes on and Willy Lewis had a diamond about seven carats and gold, and that was it, and the bags, and Egyptian -- Egypt is known for their beautiful leather work. We had bags, beautiful and in Egypt your tailors are East Indian tailors. They are in there and we went into one bar and spending money so fast the police come and put us in jail, put us in jail, because we were spending money so fast.

In fact, I think Burns or somebody went out and told them to keep coming to have some champagne. Then they found out that we're going to work at a place called the Daskin Tabris (phonetic) so they let us go, and we ran amuk there. (unintelligible) and the dancing, those European dances, everybody's working there. Everybody wouldn't / see each other--- One time he called rehearsal because we had to do a radio show and fellows, we would like to have -- don't bother me, I got to see my lawyer, don't ever bother me, I got to go and see my stockbroker. They were so busy doing everything, but living.

So, he was afraid anyway. He was back there on a prayer, so we stayed in Holland. Now, we're hearing rumors, those awful rumors, this is the last of '36, through there, '37 and Hitler's taking care of business. The Dutchmen are saying well, he's not coming through here, He's right next to them, but the Dutchmen will fight to kingdom come, that's the type of people they are.
